metadata.title: Nvidia shares slide as US tech giant investigates CEO's affair with suspected Chinese spy

left: Nvidia shares fell roughly 7% after CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged an extramarital affair and the company announced an investigation into reports that he was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.
Nvidia said its board had “no reason to believe” that national security or company secrets were compromised, but would examine all available information.
The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence determined a business executive was gathering information for China, while China’s Foreign Ministry called the allegations a smear campaign.
Analyst Dan Ives said Huang was central to Nvidia’s success and warned that the investigation could create a near-term overhang on the company’s shares.
center: Nvidia shares fell approximately 7% on Monday following reports about CEO Jensen Huang's personal life and a possible foreign intelligence investigation.
The company is investigating reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
The decline comes amid growing concerns about the sustainability of AI investments and data center expansion, causing technology stocks to fall.
Nvidia shares are down more than 20% from their peak, while the Nasdaq entered correction territory after dropping over 10% from its recent high.
right: Nvidia shares fell sharply after the company opened an independent investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.
Jensen Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and apologized, while Nvidia’s board said it had no reason to believe company or U.S. national-security information had been compromised.

Reports linked Huang to Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive whom U.S. authorities reportedly identified as a Chinese intelligence asset; China called the allegations “entirely baseless vilification and smearing.”
Madison Huang canceled planned meetings in Seoul, but South Korea expected no disruption to contracted Nvidia chip deliveries.
